verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: (5:20)[NOTE:1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:2]
notes: Beginning with 6:1, the verse numbers through 6:30 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 6:1 ET = 5:20 HT, 6:2 ET = 5:21 HT, 6:8 ET = 6:1 HT, etc., through 6:30 ET = 6:23 HT. Beginning with 7:1 the verse numbers in the English text and Hebrew text are again the same.

This paragraph is Lev 6:1-7 in the English Bible but Lev 5:20-26 in the Hebrew text. The quotation introduced by v. 1 extends from Lev 6:2 (5:21 HT) through 6:7 (5:26 HT), encompassing the third main section of guilt offering regulations. Compare the notes on Lev 1:1; 4:1; and 5:14 above.

verses.zh: 「若有人犯罪，干犯耶和华，在邻舍交付他的物上，或是在交易上行了诡诈，或是抢夺人的财物，或是欺压邻舍，
verses.en: “When a person sins and commits a trespass[NOTE:1] against the Lord by deceiving his fellow citizen[NOTE:2] in regard to something held in trust, or a pledge, or something stolen, or by extorting something from his fellow citizen,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “trespasses a trespass” (verb and direct object from the same Hebrew root מַעַל, maʿal). See the note on 5:15.
Or “neighbor” (ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NASB “companion”; TEV “a fellow-Israelite.”
Heb “has extorted his neighbor”; ASV “oppressed”; NRSV “defrauded.”

verses.zh: 或是在捡了遗失的物上行了诡诈，说谎起誓，在这一切的事上犯了甚么罪；
verses.en: or has found something lost and denies it and swears falsely[NOTE:1] concerning any one of the things that someone might do to sin[NOTE:2]—
notes: Heb “and swears on falsehood”; cf. CEV “deny something while under oath.”
Heb “on one from all which the man shall do to sin in them.”

verses.zh: 他既犯了罪，有了过犯，就要归还他所抢夺的，或是因欺压所得的，或是人交付他的，或是人遗失他所捡的物，
verses.en: when it happens that he sins and he is found guilty,[NOTE:1] then he must return whatever he had stolen, or whatever he had extorted, or the thing that he had held in trust,[NOTE:2] or the lost thing that he had found,
notes: Heb “and it shall happen, when he sins and becomes guilty,” which is both resumptive of the previous (vv. 2-3) and the conclusion to the protasis (cf. “then” introducing the next clause as the apodosis). In this case, “becomes guilty” (cf. NASB, NIV84) probably refers to his legal status as one who has been convicted of a crime in court; thus the translation “he is found guilty.” See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 1:559-61.
Heb “that had been held in trust with him.”

verses.zh: 或是他因甚么物起了假誓，就要如数归还，另外加上五分之一，在查出他有罪的日子要交还本主。
verses.en: or anything about which he swears falsely.[NOTE:1] He must restore it in full[NOTE:2] and add one-fifth to it; he must give it to its owner when he is found guilty.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “or from all which he swears on it to falsehood.”
Heb “in its head.” This refers “the full amount” in terms of the “principal,” the original item or amount obtained illegally (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:338; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 84).

Heb “to whom it is to him he shall give it in the day of his being guilty.” The present translation is based on the view that he has been found guilty through the legal process (see the note on v. 4 above; cf., e.g., TEV and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 33-34). Others translate the latter part as “in the day he presents his guilt [reparation] offering” (e.g., NIV84 and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 73, 84), or “in the day he realizes his guilt” (e.g., NRSV and J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:319, 338).

verses.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，把赎愆祭牲―就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊―牵到耶和华面前，给祭司为赎愆祭。
verses.en: Then he must bring his guilt offering to the Lord, a flawless ram from the flock, convertible into silver shekels,[NOTE:1] for a guilt offering to the priest.
notes: The words “into silver shekels” are supplied here. See the full expression in Lev 5:15, and compare 5:18. Cf. NRSV “or its equivalent”; NLT “or the animal’s equivalent value in silver.”

verses.zh: 祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪；他无论行了甚么事，使他有了罪，都必蒙赦免。」
verses.en: So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:1] on his behalf before the Lord and he will be forgiven[NOTE:2] for whatever he has done to become guilty.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Regarding “make atonement” see the note on Lev 1:4.
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV similar).
Heb “on one from all which he does to become guilty in it”; NAB “whatever guilt he may have incurred.”

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: (6:1)[NOTE:1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:2]
notes: Lev 6:8 in the English Bible = 6:1 in the Hebrew text. See also the note on 6:1.

The following paragraphs are Lev 6:8-30 in the English Bible but 6:1-23 in the Hebrew text. This initial verse makes the special priestly regulations for the people’s burnt and grain offerings into a single unit (i.e., Lev 6:8-18 [6:1-11 HT]; cf. Lev 1-2 above). Note also the separate introductions for various priestly regulations in Lev 6:19 [12 HT], 24 [17 HT], and for the common people in Lev 7:22, 28 below.

verses.zh: 「你要吩咐亚伦和他的子孙说，燔祭的条例乃是这样：燔祭要放在坛的柴上，从晚上到天亮，坛上的火要常常烧着。
verses.en: “Command Aaron and his sons, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth[NOTE:1] on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar must be kept burning on it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “It is the burnt offering on the hearth.”
Heb “in it.” In this context “in it” apparently refers to the “hearth” which was on top of the altar.

verses.zh: 祭司要穿上细麻布衣服，又要把细麻布裤子穿在身上，把坛上所烧的燔祭灰收起来，倒在坛的旁边；
verses.en: Then the priest must put on his linen robe and must put linen leggings[NOTE:1] over his bare flesh, and he must take up the fatty ashes of the burnt offering that the fire consumed on the altar,[NOTE:2] and he must place them[NOTE:3] beside the altar.
notes: The exact nature of this article of the priest’s clothing is difficult to determine. Cf. KJV, ASV “breeches”; NAB “drawers”; NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “undergarments”; NCV “underclothes”; CEV “underwear”; TEV “shorts.”
Heb “he shall lift up the fatty ashes which the fire shall consume the burnt offering on the altar.”
Heb “it,” referring the “fatty ashes” as a single unit.

verses.zh: 随后要脱去这衣服，穿上别的衣服，把灰拿到营外洁净之处。
verses.en: Then he must take off his clothes and put on other clothes, and he must bring the fatty ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean[NOTE:1] place,
notes: The word “ceremonially” has been supplied in the translation to clarify that the uncleanness of the place involved is ritual or ceremonial in nature.

verses.zh: 坛上的火要在其上常常烧着，不可熄灭。祭司要每日早晨在上面烧柴，并要把燔祭摆在坛上，在其上烧平安祭牲的脂油。
verses.en: but the fire which is on the altar must be kept burning on it.[NOTE:1] It must not be extinguished. So the priest must kindle wood on it morning by morning, and he must arrange the burnt offering on it and offer the fat of the peace offering up in smoke on it.
notes: Heb “in it,” apparently referring to the “hearth” which was on top of the altar (cf. the note on v. 9).

verses.zh: 在坛上必有常常烧着的火，不可熄灭。」
verses.en: A continual fire must be kept burning on the altar. It must not be extinguished.

verses.zh: 「素祭的条例乃是这样：亚伦的子孙要在坛前把这祭献在耶和华面前。
verses.en: “‘This is the law of the grain offering. The sons of Aaron are to present it[NOTE:1] before the Lord in front of the altar,
notes: Heb “offering it, the sons of Aaron.” The verb is a Hiphil infinitive absolute, which is used here in place of the finite verb as either a jussive (GKC 346 §113.cc, “let the sons of Aaron offer”) or more likely an injunctive in light of the verbs that follow (Joüon 2:430 §123.v, “the sons of Aaron shall/must offer”).

verses.zh: 祭司要从其中―就是从素祭的细面中―取出自己的一把，又要取些油和素祭上所有的乳香，烧在坛上，奉给耶和华为馨香素祭的纪念。
verses.en: and the priest[NOTE:1] must take up with his hand some of the choice wheat flour of the grain offering[NOTE:2] and some of its olive oil, and all of the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and he must offer its memorial portion[NOTE:3] up in smoke on the altar[NOTE:4] as a soothing aroma to the Lord.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity. The “he” refers to the officiating priest. A similar shift between singular and plural occurs in Lev 1:7-9, but see the note on Lev 1:7 and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 89 for the possibility of a textual defect.
Heb “shall take up from it with his hand some of the choice wheat flour of the grain offering.”
See the note on Lev 2:2.
Smr reading, which includes the locative ה (he, translated “on” the altar), is preferred here. This is the normal construction with the verb “offer up in smoke” in Lev 1-7 (see the note on Lev 1:9).
Heb “and he shall offer up in smoke [on] the altar a soothing aroma, its memorial portion, to the Lord.”

verses.zh: 所剩下的，亚伦和他子孙要吃，必在圣处不带酵而吃，要在会幕的院子里吃。
verses.en: Aaron and his sons are to eat what is left over from it. It must be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Meeting Tent.

verses.zh: 烤的时候不可搀酵。这是从所献给我的火祭中赐给他们的分，是至圣的，和赎罪祭并赎愆祭一样。
verses.en: It must not be baked with yeast.[NOTE:1] I have given it as their portion from my gifts. It is most holy,[NOTE:2] like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
notes: Heb “It must not be baked leavened” (cf. Lev 2:11). The noun “leaven” is traditional in English versions (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV), but “yeast” is more commonly used today.
Heb “holiness of holinesses [or holy of holies] it is”; cf. NAB “most sacred.”

verses.zh: 凡献给耶和华的火祭，亚伦子孙中的男丁都要吃这一分，直到万代，作他们永得的分。摸这些祭物的，都要成为圣。」
verses.en: Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. It is a perpetual allotted portion[NOTE:1] throughout your generations[NOTE:2] from the gifts of the Lord. Anyone who touches these gifts[NOTE:3] must be holy.’”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “a perpetual regulation”; cf. NASB “a permanent ordinance”; NRSV “as their perpetual due.”
Heb “for your generations”; cf. NIV11 “for all generations to come.”
Heb “touches them”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity. In this context “them” must refer to the “gifts” of the Lord.

Or “anyone/anything that touches them shall become holy” (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:443-56). The question is whether this refers to the contagious nature of holy objects (cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT) or whether it simply sets forth a demand that anyone who touches the holy gifts of the Lord must be a holy person (cf. CEV). See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:900-902.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 6:8 [6:1 HT] above.

verses.zh: 「当亚伦受膏的日子，他和他子孙所要献给耶和华的供物，就是细面伊法十分之一，为常献的素祭：早晨一半，晚上一半。
verses.en: “This is the offering of Aaron and his sons which they must present to the Lord on the day when he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah[NOTE:1] of choice wheat flour[NOTE:2] as a continual grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
notes: A tenth of an ephah is about 2.3 liters, one day’s ration for a single person (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:306).
For the rendering “choice wheat flour” see the note on Lev 2:1.

verses.zh: 要在铁鏊上用油调和做成，调匀了，你就拿进来；烤好了分成块子，献给耶和华为馨香的素祭。
verses.en: It must be made with olive oil on a griddle, and you must bring it well soaked,[NOTE:1] so you must present a grain offering of broken pieces[NOTE:2] as a soothing aroma to the Lord.
notes: The term rendered here “well soaked” (see, e.g., NRSV; the Hebrew term is מֻרְבֶּכֶת, murbekhet) occurs only three times (here; 7:12, and 1 Chr 23:29), and is sometimes translated “well-mixed” (e.g., NIV, NCV, NLT; NASB “well stirred”; NAB “well kneaded”). The meaning is uncertain (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:399-400), but in Lev 7:12 it stands parallel to already prepared grain offerings either “mixed” (the Hebrew term is בְּלוּלֹת (belulot), not מֻרְבֶּכֶת as in Lev 6:21 [6:14 HT]) or anointed with oil.

Heb “broken bits [?] of a grain offering of pieces,” but the meaning of the Hebrew term rendered here “broken bits” (תֻּפִינֵי, tufine) is quite uncertain. Some take it from the Hebrew verb “to break up, to crumble” (פַּת [pat]; e.g., the Syriac, NAB, NIV, NLT “broken” pieces) and others from “to bake” (אָפַה, ʾafah; e.g., NRSV “baked pieces”). For a good summary of other proposed options, see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 90. Compare Lev 2:5-6 for the general regulations regarding this manner of grain offering. Similar but less problematic terminology is used there.

verses.zh: 亚伦的子孙中，接续他为受膏的祭司，要把这素祭献上，要全烧给耶和华。这是永远的定例。
verses.en: The high priest who succeeds him[NOTE:1] from among his sons must do it. It is a perpetual statute; it must be offered up in smoke as a whole offering to the Lord.
notes: Heb “And the anointed priest under him.”

verses.zh: 祭司的素祭都要烧了，却不可吃。」
verses.en: Every grain offering of a priest must be a whole offering; it must not be eaten.”

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 6:8 [6:1 HT].

verses.zh: 「你对亚伦和他的子孙说，赎罪祭的条例乃是这样：要在耶和华面前、宰燔祭牲的地方宰赎罪祭牲；这是至圣的。
verses.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons, ‘This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered the sin offering must be slaughtered before the Lord. It is most holy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “holiness of holinesses [or holy of holies] it is.” Cf. NAB “most sacred”; CEV “very sacred”; TEV “very holy.”

verses.zh: 为赎罪献这祭的祭司要吃，要在圣处，就是在会幕的院子里吃。
verses.en: The priest who offers it for sin is to eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Meeting Tent.

verses.zh: 凡摸这祭肉的要成为圣；这祭牲的血若弹在甚么衣服上，所弹的那一件要在圣处洗净。
verses.en: Anyone who touches its meat must be holy, and whoever spatters some of its blood on a garment[NOTE:1] must wash[NOTE:2] whatever he spatters it on in a holy place.
notes: Heb “on the garment”; NCV “on any clothes”; CEV “on the clothes of the priest.”

The translation “you must wash” is based on the MT as it stands (cf. NASB, NIV). Smr, LXX, Syriac, Tg. Ps.-J., and the Vulgate have a third person masculine singular passive form (Pual), “[the garment] must be washed” (cf. NAB, NRSV, NLT). This could also be supported from the verbs in the following verse, and it requires only a repointing of the Hebrew text with no change in consonants. See the remarks in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 90 and J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:404.

verses.zh: 惟有煮祭物的瓦器要打碎；若是煮在铜器里，这铜器要擦磨，在水中涮净。
verses.en: Any clay vessel it is boiled in must be broken, and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, then that vessel[NOTE:1] must be rubbed out and rinsed in water.
notes: Heb “it”; the words “that vessel” are supplied in the translation to clarify the referent.

verses.zh: 凡祭司中的男丁都可以吃；这是至圣的。
verses.en: Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “holiness of holinesses [or holy of holies] it is” (also in 7:1).

verses.zh: 凡赎罪祭，若将血带进会幕在圣所赎罪，那肉都不可吃，必用火焚烧。」
verses.en: But any sin offering from which some of its blood is brought into the Meeting Tent to make atonement in the sanctuary must not be eaten. It must be burned up in the fire.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “burned with fire,” an expression which is sometimes redundant in English, but here means “burned up,” “burned up entirely.”
